key_insight: A small periodic rocking motion superimposed on vertical bath vibration can steer bouncing droplets laterally, with velocity set by rocking amplitude and phase.
engineering_relevance: This offers a simple programmable control knob for manipulating passive or active droplets in pilot-wave and related fluidic transport systems.
method: Add a low-amplitude periodic rocking motion to the usual vertical forcing of the liquid bath.
Measure how droplet lateral velocity changes with rocking amplitude α and phase φ relative to the vertical drive.
Model the droplet as a harmonic bouncer to predict an average lateral force: F̄x = mgα sin(Φb + φ).
evidence_signal: Experiments show lateral velocity varies linearly with rocking amplitude and sinusoidally with phase, with a strong dependence on the droplet’s vertical bouncing mode.
watch_item: The response depends strongly on the bouncing mode, so the control law may need recalibration across different droplet states and impact phases.
paper_title: Phase-controlled lateral forcing of droplets on a vibrating bath
